data.name: Settings_TopmostTip
data.value: While game is active (at first): the overlay stays on top while the game's window is in front; other windows can cover it. Always: on top of every window. Never: an ordinary window that the game and other windows cover when they're in front.

data.name: Settings_SceneKindTip
data.value: All fights (at first): the meter counts everything from the last reset or map change on, trash included. Boss battles only: it counts only while a boss is fought and keeps that fight shown until the next boss; each goes into the history on its own. Switching puts the current fight into the history.

data.name: Settings_MainMetricVisibilityTip
data.value: Which columns the meter's table and its boss fights show, and the total DPS in the bottom bar. The numbers say how many of them are shown.

data.name: Settings_MainMetricVisibility_DamagePerSecondTip
data.value: Each player's damage per second in the fight. Shown at first.

data.name: Settings_MainMetricVisibility_DamageTip
data.value: Each player's total damage in the fight. Shown at first.

data.name: Settings_MainMetricVisibility_HealingPerSecondTip
data.value: Each player's healing per second, with or without overhealing (General tab). Hidden at first.

data.name: Settings_MainMetricVisibility_HealingTip
data.value: Each player's total healing, with or without overhealing (General tab). Hidden at first.

data.name: Settings_MainMetricVisibility_OverhealingTip
data.value: Show (at first): healing and HPS count every heal in full, overhealing included. Hide: only the HP a heal actually restored. For the meter, the player details and the fight graphs.

data.name: Settings_MainMetricVisibility_DamageTakenTip
data.value: The damage each player took. Hidden at first.

data.name: Settings_MainMetricVisibility_UnhealedHealthTip
data.value: Missing HP × seconds: how much of a player's health stayed missing, and for how long. Lower is better for a healer; everyone's added up is in the bottom bar. Hidden at first.

data.name: Settings_MainMetricVisibility_Aggro
data.value: Aggro (share of enemy casts aimed at the player)

data.name: Settings_MainMetricVisibility_AggroTip
data.value: Auto: shown while your character is a Gladiator or Templar. A click goes through Auto, Show and Hide.

data.name: Settings_MainMetricVisibility_RecoveryTimeTip
data.value: Auto: shown while your character is a Cleric. A click goes through Auto, Show and Hide.

data.name: Settings_BossTimeLimitTip
data.value: With a limit, each boss fight shows the DPS still needed to kill the boss in time (its HP left ÷ the time left) against the group's DPS on it: green ahead, red behind, also in the bottom bar. Off at first.

data.name: Settings_MainMetricVisibility_TotalDamagePerSecondTip
data.value: The damage per second of everyone in the meter, added up, in its bottom bar. Shown at first.

data.name: Settings_TimeDisplayFormatTip
data.value: How times are written in the meter's bottom bar and boss fights, the player details and the skill monitor: 68.3s (at first) or 01:08.

data.name: Settings_MainMetricsCompactTip
data.value: On (at first): numbers from 1,000 up are shortened to three digits with k, m or b (12.3k, 1.23m). Off: in full (12,345). For the meter's columns, its bottom bar, the boss fights and the target status bar.

data.name: Settings_FocusStatusBarTip
data.value: On (at first): at the top of the meter a bar for each boss in the fight, with its name, HP and stagger gauge, and under it the section of the boss fight going on. Off: neither; the fight waits in the list of boss fights below the table.

data.name: Settings_ShowPlayerNamesTip
data.value: Show (at first): character names. Hide: each player's class and a number instead (Cleric 1).

data.name: Settings_PlayerNameSettingsTip
data.value: How players are named in the meter, the details, the playback and the fight graphs.

data.name: Settings_PlayerSelfMarkerTip
data.value: A ⭐ before your own name: always, only while names are hidden (at first), or never.

data.name: Settings_PlayerShortServerNameTip
data.value: Each player's server, shortened, after their name: Name[Server]. Hidden at first.

data.name: Settings_PlayerLegionNameTip

data.name: Settings_PlayerFactionTintTip

data.name: Settings_SkillMonitor_EnableTip
data.value: On: the frame shows. Off: it's closed, and its settings stay as they are. Its button in the meter's title bar turns it on and off too.

data.name: Settings_GroupFrame_MyBuffsTip
data.value: Your own buffs and HoTs on each member, with their time left. Shown at first.

data.name: Settings_GroupFrame_DebuffsTip
data.value: The debuff icons on each member. A violet frame still marks a debuffed member with them hidden. Shown at first.

data.name: Settings_GroupFrame_OtherBuffsTip
data.value: Buffs other players cast on each member. Hidden at first.

data.name: Settings_GroupFrame_PermanentBuffsTip
data.value: Buffs without a timer (or with more than an hour left), yours and others'; debuffs aren't affected. Shown at first.

data.name: Settings_GroupFrame_ItemBuffsTip
data.value: Buffs from scrolls, food and drinks, and from other items you use up, such as potions and talismans, yours and others'. Theostone procs and debuffs aren't affected. Shown at first.

data.name: Settings_GroupFrame_AuraSideTip
data.value: Where each member's buffs and debuffs go: right of the HP bar (at first), left of it (the frame then grows to the left) or nowhere. A click moves on to the next.

data.name: Settings_GroupFrame_AuraOpacityTip
data.value: How see-through the buffs and debuffs are: 100 % (at first) is their own look, lower fades them, down to 10 %.

data.name: Settings_GroupFrame_ShieldBarTip
data.value: The end of the HP bar the shields start from: left (at first) or right.

data.name: Settings_GroupFrame_ShieldAnimationTip
data.value: On (at first): each shield on its own, blinking for its last 3 s. Off: one bar for all shields, without blinking.

data.name: Settings_GroupFrame_DeathsTip
data.value: Each member's deaths in the current boss fight, beside their name. Shown at first.

data.name: Settings_GroupFrame_ArrowSideTip
data.value: Where each member's direction arrow goes: right of the HP bar (at first), left of it or nowhere. A click moves on to the next.

data.name: Settings_GroupFrame_DistanceSideTip
data.value: Where each member's distance in metres goes: right of the HP bar (at first), left of it or nowhere. A click moves on to the next.

data.name: Settings_GroupFrame_DistanceGreenTip
data.value: A member's distance shows green up to this. 25 m at first.

data.name: Settings_GroupFrame_DistanceOrangeTip
data.value: Past green, the distance shows orange up to this. 35 m at first.

data.name: Settings_GroupFrame_DistanceRangeTip
data.value: Past orange, the distance shows red up to this; farther away a member is out of range and dimmed. 40 m at first.

data.name: Settings_HiddenCubes_SoundTip
data.value: A blip when a new Hidden Cube shows up in the frame, at the boss alert's volume. Off at first.

data.name: Settings_GroupFrame_AlertEnabled
data.value: Sound when the boss targets you

data.name: Settings_GroupFrame_AlertEnabledTip
data.value: On: a sound plays when a boss turns to you, as the group frame shows "⚠ Boss targets you"; not again within the quiet time. Needs the group frame on. Off at first.

data.name: Settings_GroupFrame_AlertSoundTip
data.value: The sound the alert plays: the chime (at first), knock, blip or one of your own (the last five added). Picking one plays it.

data.name: Settings_GroupFrame_AlertAddTip
data.value: Cuts a sound of up to 10 s from a sound or video file (mp3, mp4, …) in an editor and adds it under a name of yours.

data.name: Settings_GroupFrame_AlertQuietTip

data.name: Settings_GroupFrame_AlertPlayTip
data.value: Plays the alert's sound at this volume, to try it.

data.name: AlertEditor_Unreadable
data.value: Windows can't read any sound from this file.

data.name: AlertEditor_Hint
data.value: Drag the yellow edges, or click near one to move it there; ←/→ move it by 10 ms (Shift: 100 ms). At most 10 s.

data.name: Settings_Debug_StartRecordingTip
data.value: Records everything the game server sends, for a bug report: the recording can be played back to see what went wrong. It runs until you stop or save it; starting again starts over, and an unsaved recording is lost.

data.name: Settings_Debug_SavePacketsTip
data.value: Ends the recording and saves it where you pick, as a .aion2healdebug file to send with a bug report.

data.name: Settings_SkillMonitor_SelectAllTip
data.value: Ticks every skill of every class for this, also skills that come with later game updates, as at first.

data.name: Settings_SkillMonitor_ClearAllTip
data.value: Unticks every skill for this: the skill monitor then shows it for none.

data.name: Settings_VisibleRowsTip

data.name: Settings_CombatantStatisticsScopeTip
data.value: Which players the meter lists: only you, your party, your whole force, or everyone in the fight (at first).

data.name: Settings_LanguageTip
data.value: The overlay's language. Names from the game (skills, bosses, maps) follow it in English, Korean and German; with Chinese they stay English. At first the Windows language (English when the overlay doesn't have it).

data.name: Settings_UiScaleTip
data.value: The size of the DPS meter and its details, the settings and the playback; each frame has a Scale of its own. 100 % at first; it changes once you let go of the slider.

data.name: Settings_OverlayOpacityTip
data.value: The look of the meter and its ping graph: at 60 % (at first) a see-through panel with text at full strength; above, the panel fills in until it's solid at 100 %; below, the whole meter fades, down to barely visible at 20 %.

data.name: Settings_FrameOpacityTip
data.value: How see-through the whole frame is: 100 % (at first) is its own look, lower fades it, down to 20 %.

data.name: Settings_DetailOpacityTip
data.value: Like Opacity, for the player details (a click on a player's row). 60 % at first.

data.name: Settings_Hotkey_BattleResetTip
data.value: Like the meter's reset button: the current fight goes into the history and the meter starts empty.

data.name: Settings_Hotkey_MinimizeAllTip
data.value: Folds the meter and every frame like their eye; pressed again while all are folded, they all come back.

data.name: Frame_MinimizeTip
data.value: Minimize: only the title line stays; click again to show everything

data.name: Meter_MinimizeTip
data.value: Minimize: only the title bar and the bottom bar stay; click again to show everything

data.name: Frame_CloseTip
data.value: Close: turns the frame off (on again from the meter's title bar or the settings)

data.name: Frame_ClickableOnTip
data.value: Clickable without focus: on. This frame takes clicks while the game has focus. Click to let the mouse through it to the game instead.

data.name: Frame_ClickableOffTip
data.value: Clickable without focus: off. While the game has focus, the mouse goes through this frame to the game, except over its title line while "Title line always clickable" is on. Click to make it take clicks instead.

data.name: Settings_Hotkey_MeterClickableTip
data.value: Switches the meter's hand: whether the meter takes clicks while the game has focus (Clickable without focus).

data.name: Settings_Hotkey_RegistrationUnavailable
data.value: Shortcut unavailable. Choose another key combination.

data.name: Settings_Hotkeys_Hint
data.value: • To set or change a shortcut, click its row and press Ctrl, Alt, Shift or Win together with one more key, such as Ctrl+Shift+R; a key on its own isn't taken. Esc leaves the shortcut as it was. • To clear a shortcut, click the × at the right of its row; the row then shows None. • Keys another row has must be cleared there first. If a row stays on Press keys…, it doesn't get those keys: another row or this one has them, Windows or another program uses them, or the key isn't supported. • Shortcuts work in every program while the overlay runs, the game included, so pick keys you don't need elsewhere.

data.name: GroupFrame_EffectLevel

data.name: GroupFrame_EffectPicksUnknown
data.value: Which of these the caster picked isn't known.

data.value: The way there, as seen facing the way you're moving, tipped up or down as it lies above or below you (green: above, red: below, blue: level). No arrow yet: move a few metres first, the game doesn't say which way you face.

data.name: Settings_Update_NowTip
data.value: Looks for a new version now; if there is one, downloads it and restarts the overlay into it. One already downloaded restarts at once.

data.name: Settings_Update_AutomaticallyTip
data.value: On: at every start, and when you switch it on, the overlay looks for a new version and downloads it; it's installed when the overlay closes. Off (at first): only Update now updates.

data.name: Settings_PatchNotesTip
data.value: The version whose patch notes show below, the newest first: what changed, first in short, then in detail (up to 1.0.74 in detail only). The version you have installed is marked and shows at first.

data.name: Settings_PatchNotesEnglish
data.value: The patch notes are in English.

data.name: Settings_DigitalTwinsTip
data.value: On: party members are looked up on the game's official character website (aion2.plaync.com) by name and server as they show up in the meter: gear, Daevanion boards, skill levels and stats, shown in the details' Digital twin tab. Off: only the players you look up there yourself.

data.name: Settings_TwinLookupPauseTip
data.value: How long the overlay waits before each call to the official character website. Looking a player up takes about 34 calls: about a minute at 0.7 s, and each second more adds about half a minute. 0.7 s at first, in steps of 0.1 s.

data.name: Settings_TwinLookupPauseWarning
data.value: A shorter pause raises the risk of being blocked by NCSOFT's website.

data.name: Status_PortIdle

data.name: Buffs_None
data.value: No buffs in this stretch yet.

data.value: Of the time the other group members could have had it (in range, or with the buff on), the share they had it. Time dead or out of sight without it counts for nothing.

data.name: Twin_NotLookedUp
data.value: Not looked up yet. "Look up" asks the game's official character website for this player; with Settings → Digital twins on, party members are looked up automatically.

data.name: Twin_Loading

data.name: Twin_NotFound

data.name: Twin_Unsupported
data.value: Only characters on the global servers (NA, EU, Asia, Latin America) can be looked up.

data.name: Twin_NoIdentity
data.value: The overlay doesn't know this player's name and server yet.

data.name: Twin_Stats
data.value: Stats from gear, Daevanion and titles

data.name: Twin_StatsNote
data.value: Sums of what the website lists, with the parts below each. Not included: the class's own base values, buffs, and the collection bonus of titles that aren't equipped.

data.name: Twin_PrimaryStats
data.value: Base stats and what they give

data.name: TwinLibrary_Note
data.value: Every digital twin looked up is kept here as it was at that moment, the newest first.

data.value: Opens a line to look up any character by server and name on the official website and add the snapshot to the library; another click closes it

data.name: TwinLibrary_Looking
data.value: Looking up {0} on {1} on the official website (about {2} min)…

data.value: Looks you up again on the official website and adds the snapshot to the library

data.name: OwnTwin_Unknown
data.value: The overlay doesn't know your character yet: it learns it at login or the next map change.

data.name: TwinLibrary_UpdateMyselfOnStartTip
data.value: Once each time the overlay starts, looks your character up again on the official website as soon as the overlay knows who you play, and adds the snapshot to the library. A character you switch to later is looked up once too. Turned on while you play, it looks you up right away. Off at first.

data.name: TwinLibrary_UseSeenLevelsTip
data.value: On: each skill shows the level the game sent for that player in your last boss fight together, in italics. The official website's level fills in only the skills that fight didn't show. The website lists just one of the three skill setups a player can switch between, while the fight shows the one they played, gear and Daevanion included. The game sends levels only with buffs, debuffs, heals and damage over time, shields and passives. A stigma's hits show how many of its specializations are unlocked, which gives its level as a range: 15–19 with three, 20+ with four, as the fifth's level isn't known. The website's level stays where it's inside that range. Other skills that only hit or heal keep the website's level. Battlefields don't count, as every level reads 20 there. On a player's Digital twin tab in the details, the levels come from the fight shown there. On at first.

data.name: TwinLibrary_FavouritesNote
data.value: Your favourite snapshots. A click on a filled ♥ takes one off.

data.name: TwinLibrary_NoFavourites
data.value: No favourites yet: click the ♥ beside a snapshot to keep it here.

data.name: TwinLibrary_CloseTip
data.value: Close: the library opens again from the meter's title bar

data.name: TwinLibrary_CompareTip
data.value: Tick two to five snapshots, then compare them side by side.

data.name: TwinLibrary_PickTip
data.value: Tick to compare (two to five) or to delete together

data.name: TwinCompare_RelativeTip
data.value: Shows how much more (+, green) or less (-, red) each snapshot has than the reference; a stat it doesn't list counts as 0. Hover a value for the number itself and the change in percent. A stigma shown as a level range from a fight has no single difference: it shows the range, and where the reference shows one, the others in that row show their levels.

data.name: TwinCompare_SortTip
data.value: Puts the stats where the others differ most from the reference first in each section; the skills are sorted within their group (active skills, passive skills, stigmas). A stat's difference is the change in percent, averaged over the others (+20%, +40% and -20% give +13.3%); a big drop counts as much as a big gain. Equal ones keep their order.

data.name: Twin_SpecializationsNote
data.value: Read from the skill ids of this player's own hits. A stigma's number shows how far its specializations are unlocked, and the ones below count too. Effects as the game words them, in English.

data.name: Twin_SeenLevelTip
data.value: Numbers for skill level {0}, {1}'s level as the game sent it in the fight of {2:g}.

data.name: Twin_SeenRangeTip
data.value: Skill level {0} in the fight of {1:g}, from the specializations its hits showed unlocked.

data.name: Twin_SeenSummary
data.value: skill levels in italics go by the fight of {0:g}

data.name: Twin_SeenLevelsNote
data.value: As the game sent them with this player's buffs, debuffs, heals and damage over time, shields and passives, gear and Daevanion included. Skills that only hit or heal never send theirs, so look the player up for those. A stigma shows a range instead (such as 15–19), from the specializations its hits show unlocked.

data.name: Settings_FightGraphs_MembersTip
data.value: A curve for each party member in every graph, besides yours and the party's. Hidden at first.

data.name: Settings_FightGraphs_OtherDeathsTip
data.value: Marks the other members' deaths in the graphs too, not only yours. Hidden at first.

data.name: Settings_FightGraphs_SmoothTip
data.value: The curves follow an average of the seconds around each (about ±5 s), so single big hits don't make them spiky; peaks stay where they were. Hovering still lists each second's own values.

data.name: Settings_FightGraphs_OverviewTip
data.value: The overview above the graphs: your own values of every metric in one chart, each scaled to its peak in the fight. Shown at first.

data.name: Settings_FightGraphs_BestMetricTip
data.value: The metric that picks your best pull of a boss, the dotted line in each graph: your best complete kill by it. DPS at first; a training dummy's best always goes by DPS.

data.name: Settings_FightGraphs_NewBestsInTitle
data.value: New best runs in the title line

data.name: Settings_FightGraphs_NewBestsInTitleTip
data.value: While the frame is folded, its title line names the metrics the shown pull set a new personal best in.

data.name: FightGraphs_BestTip
data.value: Your best complete kill of this boss by {0}: {1}, {2} long. Click to hide or show it.

data.name: FightGraphs_FirstBest
data.value: ★ First complete kill of {0}: kept as your best pull.

data.name: FightGraphs_CompareTip
data.value: Tick two to five stored runs, then compare their graphs one below the other.

data.name: FightGraphs_EqualTimeTip
data.value: On: a second is as wide in every graph, so the longest run fills the width and shorter ones end early; how long a spike lasts, or the gap between damage taken and healing, compares directly. Off: each run fills the width.

data.name: FightGraphs_StoreTip
data.value: Keeps the pull shown, with its history entry, in the Stored runs tab.

data.name: FightGraphs_StoreFailed

data.name: FightGraphs_SortTip

data.name: FightGraphs_OpenTip

data.name: FightGraphs_OpenFailed

data.name: FightGraphs_DeleteTip

data.value: * As a cleric, this is the whole group's value (everyone's missing HP, or their recovery time), not your own: your runs are ranked by it, as keeping everyone's HP up is your job.

data.name: FightGraphs_RunValuesNote
data.value: In the runs: per second of the pull, on average (aggro: the share of the pull the boss was after you; recovery time: the pull's UHS ÷ its damage taken).

data.name: Settings_ClickableWithoutFocusTip
data.value: On: the frame takes clicks while the game has focus. Off: the mouse goes through it to the game until the overlay has focus, except over its title line while "Title line always clickable" is on (by default only the DPS meter's: click its title bar to give the overlay focus).

data.name: Settings_TitleClickableTip

On: while the game has focus, the frame's title line still takes clicks (a click there gives the overlay focus) and the rest of the frame lets the mouse through to the game. data.name: Settings_Visuals_PartOpacityTip

data.name: FightGraphs_OverviewTip
data.value: Your own values, each metric scaled to its peak in this fight. Click a metric on the right to show or hide it; with none left the overview hides.

data.value: Damage per second on the boss

data.value: Boss (share of the boss's HP the player took off)

data.name: Settings_MainMetricVisibility_BossShareTip
data.value: Each player's share of the boss's HP they took off; shown while a boss is up, and after a kill until the next boss. Shown at first.

data.name: BossFocus_StaggerTip
data.value: Stagger gauge: stagger skills wear it down; at 0 the boss is staggered for about 5 s, then it refills.

data.name: Settings_MainMetricVisibility_ColumnHeadersTip
data.value: The headings above the meter's columns: hover one for what it shows, click one to sort by it (again: the other way round). Shown at first.

data.name: ColumnHeader_UnhealedHealthTip
data.value: Unhealed health seconds: missing HP × seconds

data.name: ColumnHeader_RecoveryTimeTip
data.value: Recovery time: UHS ÷ damage taken, the seconds damage stayed unhealed on average

data.name: ColumnHeader_AggroTip
data.value: Aggro: share of enemy casts aimed at this player

data.name: ColumnHeader_StaggerTip
data.value: Stagger: share of the boss stagger gauge this player wore down

data.name: ColumnHeader_KillsTip
data.value: Kills: enemies that died with this player having taken most of their HP off

data.name: ColumnHeader_LastHitsTip
data.value: Last hits: killing blows on enemies, as the game's kill message names them

data.name: ColumnHeader_CreditedTip
data.value: Credited: your kills as the game counts them (enemies you or your party hit); yours only

data.name: ColumnHeader_BossShareTip
data.value: Share of the boss's HP this player took off

data.name: BossSection_Toggle
data.value: Show or hide the players' stats in this fight

data.name: Settings_TrainingDummiesTip
data.value: A pull on a training dummy starts with your first hit and ends when you pause for the cut-off, or when its length is up. Other players' hits don't count. Only pulls that run the full length can become a personal best.

data.name: Settings_DummyPullTip
data.value: How long a training dummy pull runs. A pull that runs its full length can become a personal best for that length. Until you stop (at first): the pull ends with the pause below and sets no best.

data.name: Settings_DummyCutoffTip
data.value: A training dummy pull ends once you haven't hit the dummy for this long. 5 s at first.

data.name: FightGraphs_BestDummyTip
data.value: Your best full-length training dummy pull by {0}: {1}, {2} long. Click to hide or show it.

data.name: FightGraphs_FirstDummyBest
data.value: ★ First full-length pull on a training dummy: kept as your best pull.

data.name: Status_PingPercentileTip
data.value: In brackets: 99 % of your pings in the last 2 minutes were at or below this. The game measures one every 10 s, so it is the highest of about 12.

data.name: Status_PingGraphTip
data.value: Click for your ping over the last hour.

data.name: PingGraph_Hint
data.value: Scroll or drag to move through the last hour.

data.name: Scenes_Hint
data.value: A scene keeps which frames are open, folded or closed, where they are and where they take clicks. Apply it here, with its shortcut or by a workflow.

data.name: Scenes_Empty
data.value: No scenes yet: place the frames as you like them, then add the current scene.

data.name: Scenes_AddTip
data.value: Saves the frames as they are now as a new scene: which are open, folded or closed, where they are and where they take clicks. Type its name: Enter or a click elsewhere saves it, Esc cancels. A name you already have saves that scene anew.

data.name: Scenes_ApplyTip
data.value: Applies this scene now: each frame open, folded or closed, back where it was saved, and where it takes clicks (a dash leaves that as it is). Its shortcut and its workflows apply it the same way.

data.name: Scenes_OverwriteTip
data.value: Overwrites this scene with the frames as they are now, like a new scene: which are open, folded or closed, where they are and where they take clicks. Its name, its place in the list, its shortcut and the workflows that use it stay. The first click asks, the next one overwrites.

data.name: Scenes_DeleteTip
data.value: Deletes this scene: the first click asks, the next one deletes. Its shortcut goes with it, and the workflows that use it do nothing until you pick another scene for them.

data.name: Scenes_RenameTip
data.value: Renames this scene: Enter or a click elsewhere keeps the new name, Esc cancels. A name another scene has isn't taken. Its shortcut and its workflows stay.

data.name: Scenes_ShortcutTip
data.value: Keys that apply this scene in every program while the overlay runs, the game included. Click here, then press Ctrl, Alt, Shift or Win together with one more key; Esc leaves the shortcut as it was, the × clears it. Also under Hotkeys.

data.name: Scenes_StateTip
data.value: What the scene does with this frame. Open: shows it. Folded: shows only its title line, like its eye. Closed: turns it off, like its cross. The DPS meter has no Closed: its cross ends the overlay.

data.name: Scenes_SettingTip
data.value: Empty: the scene turns the setting off for this frame. Ticked: it turns it on. Dash: it leaves the setting as it is (older scenes show the dash). Each click moves on to the next, from the dash back to empty.

data.name: Settings_Hotkey_SaveSceneTip
data.value: Asks for a name and saves the frames as they are now as a scene; a name you already have saves that scene anew.

data.name: Settings_Hotkey_ApplySceneTip
data.value: Applies this scene: its frames open, folded or closed, where they were saved, and where they take clicks.

data.name: Scenes_SavePromptHint
data.value: Enter saves, Esc cancels. A name you already have saves that scene anew.

data.name: Workflows_Hint
data.value: When something happens in game, a workflow applies one of your scenes. A workflow that's off is kept but does nothing.

data.name: Workflows_AddTip
data.value: Adds a workflow: when a boss fight starts, it applies your first scene. Change both in its box below.

data.name: Workflows_NeedScene
data.value: A workflow applies a scene: add one under Scenes first.

data.name: Workflows_WhenTip
data.value: What sets the workflow off: a boss fight starting or ending, or you entering a dungeon.

data.name: Workflows_ApplyTip
data.value: The scene the workflow applies. If that scene is deleted, the workflow does nothing until you pick another.

data.name: Workflows_ActiveTip
data.value: Ticked: the workflow applies its scene when that happens. Unticked: it's kept but does nothing.

data.name: Workflows_DungeonTip
data.value: Dungeons are the maps with ids 600000-699999 (Krao Cave to Vakron Sky Island, hard modes, Ludra) and the tiered instances 910000-919999. Towns, fields, the Legion airships and the Shugo Festival's maps are not.

data.name: Settings_BossParticipation_Warn
data.value: Warn for too low boss participation

data.name: Settings_BossParticipation_WarnTip
data.value: On (at first): in a boss fight the group frame shows a loot bag with your share of the boss against what its loot needs: red while you'd end under it at this pace, yellow while you're on course, green once it's reached. Needs the group frame on.

data.name: Settings_BossParticipation_NeededTip
data.value: The share of the boss's HP you must take off for its loot, which the loot bag checks against. 3.5 % at first, in steps of 0.5 %.

data.name: BossParticipation_Reached
data.value: Loot: {0} of the boss, {1} needed. Reached.

data.name: BossParticipation_OnCourse
data.value: Loot: {0} of the boss so far, {1} needed. At this pace about {2} at the kill.

data.name: BossParticipation_Short
data.value: Loot: {0} of the boss so far, {1} needed. At this pace only about {2} at the kill: hit the boss more.

data.name: BossParticipation_Missed
data.value: Loot: {0} of the boss, under the {1} needed.

data.name: Tutorial_ButtonTip
data.value: Tutorial: a short tour of the overlay

data.name: Tutorial_StartTip
data.value: A short tour of the overlay with a made-up fight. Nothing of yours changes, and your frames are back as they were at the end.

data.name: Tutorial_Welcome_Text
data.value: This tour shows the overlay with a made-up fight: HappyCat, a cleric (she is "you" for the tour), and her group against Vakron. Nothing of yours is changed, and your layout comes back at the end. Go on with Next, or stop with End tour at any time.

data.name: Tutorial_Rows_Text
data.value: Each row is a player of the fight shown, here the tour's entry in the history. The bar is their share of the column you sort by; your own row is HappyCat's.

data.name: Tutorial_Sorting_Text
data.value: Click a column heading to sort by it, click it again to turn the order round. Hover over a value to see what it means. Settings → DPS meter chooses the columns.

data.name: Tutorial_Uhs_Text
data.value: Missing HP times seconds: how much health stayed missing, and for how long. Lower is better for a healer; the whole group's is in the bottom bar. Recovery time (Rec., shown for clerics) is UHS ÷ damage taken: how many seconds damage stayed unhealed on average.

data.name: Tutorial_Details_Text
data.value: A click on a row opens the details: skills with hits, crits and targets, healing, damage taken and buffs. Here HappyCat's, with her heals, HoT ticks and shields.

data.name: Tutorial_BossSection_Text
data.value: Each pull of a boss gets a section of its own: the numbers of this pull only, the DPS check (green ahead, red behind), and every pull in the list below, wipes included.

data.name: Tutorial_History_Text
data.value: Earlier fights stay here: open one to see it in the meter, rename it, export it or play it back. The tour's fight is in here too while the tour runs.

data.name: Tutorial_Playback_Text
data.value: The fight event by event: play it, jump on the timeline, step from event to event. The meter and the fight graphs follow the moment shown.

data.name: Tutorial_Ping_Text
data.value: Your ping, and in brackets what 99 % of the last two minutes stayed under. A click opens the last hour's graph; it stays open until you click again.

data.name: Tutorial_Hand_Text
data.value: Every frame has a hand like this one at the meter's bottom right, shown while the overlay has focus. A hand: the frame takes clicks even while the game has focus. Crossed out: the mouse goes through the frame to the game then. A click on the hand switches it. A frame with "Title line always clickable" on (in its settings; at first only the meter) still takes clicks on its title line: a click on the meter's title bar gives the overlay focus.

data.name: Tutorial_Frames_Text
data.value: These buttons turn the frames on and off: the group frame, the skill monitor, the fight graphs, the Hidden Cubes and the twin library. Gold means on.

data.name: Tutorial_GroupFrame_Text
data.value: Your group's HP and shields, a red frame around whom the boss targets, violet for a debuff, a cross for deaths, and your HoTs and buffs with their time left. Here the group at the end of the fight.

data.name: Tutorial_LootBag_Text
data.value: Your share of the boss against what its loot needs (3.5 % at first): red while you'd stay under it, yellow while you're on course, green once it's reached. Hover over it for the numbers.

data.name: Tutorial_TitleClick_Text
data.value: While the overlay has focus, a click on a frame's title line folds it down to that line, like the eye; another click brings it back. Drag the line to move the frame; the cross turns it off.

data.name: Tutorial_SkillMonitor_Text
data.value: Your buffs and cooldowns at a glance, and your debuffs on your target in a violet frame. Settings → Skill monitor chooses which skills it shows.

data.name: Tutorial_FightGraphs_Text
data.value: Each pull as graphs over time, with your best pull as a dotted line. Store a run to keep it and compare it with others later.

data.name: Tutorial_TwinLibrary_Text
data.value: Gear, stats and skills of players, looked up on the official site and kept here. HappyCat is made up and goes again after the tour. Compare puts twins side by side: green is better, red worse.

data.name: Tutorial_Scenes_Text
data.value: Save how your frames are laid out (open, folded or closed, and where) and where they take clicks, then switch between scenes with a click or a shortcut.

data.name: Tutorial_Workflows_Text
data.value: Let the overlay switch scenes by itself: when a boss fight starts or ends, or when you enter a dungeon.

data.name: Tutorial_Shortcuts_Text
data.value: Keys that work while the game has focus: the reset, the meter's hand (clickable without focus), minimizing all frames, and saving or applying a scene.

data.name: Tutorial_Done_Text
data.value: Your layout comes back now. The tour can be started again here, in Settings → General. Have a good fight!
